inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average shares for Q2 2026 (10-Q filed 2026-07-16, us-gaap WeightedAverageNumberOfDilutedSharesOutstanding 1,150,281,044); issued shares 1,147.5M. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, and option exercises (~$10M/half) are offset by small buybacks ($50.3M H1-2026), so the count has been flat within 0.3% for three years.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest and other income was $5.5M in FY2025 (10-K) on a net-cash position of ~$15M; net cash is ~1% of the FCF base, far below the 1x materiality threshold, so it is left in the flows and the cash is added to EV once.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement stock-based compensation add-back $8.4M (XBRL ShareBasedCompensation); no separate equity-award tax withholding line is disclosed and Fastenal publishes no adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, so the add-back is the whole charge. SBC is 0.10% of revenue: the house/street band is ~$0.60/share wide.
inputs.buyback_note: H1-2026 repurchases $50.3M (Q1 $20.3M, Q2 $30.0M); zero in FY2023, FY2024 and FY2025. Fastenal returns cash mainly through dividends ($1,004M FY2025, $551M H1-2026), ~96% of owner FCF. The flat count is funded: option-exercise dilution is tiny and buybacks cover it.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:01Z regular close (Friday); Yahoo chart API, not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD discount rate. Cost of equity ~9.2% = 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.0 x ERP 5.0%; debt is <0.5% of capital so WACC rounds to 9.0%. Below the 10.5% US-tech default because Fastenal is a 60-year-old distributor with no leverage, 20%+ operating margins through every cycle since 2009, and 30%+ ROIC. Risk is charged ONCE: cyclicality, tariff margin pressure and the CEO transition live in the scenario flows and weights, and the same 9.0% is used for all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) leases as operating cost, by construction. Fastenal reports under US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost ($128.1M FY2025, cash payments $125.3M) is already inside operating expenses and therefore inside reported EBITDA and OCF, so no lease_cost_pct_path is charged and the $316.9M operating lease liability is EXCLUDED from net debt. Charging either would double-count.
inputs.nci_treatment: None: Fastenal has no non-controlling interests.
inputs.working_capital_note: Distributor sign: operating NWC (receivables $1,557M + inventory $1,735M - payables $400M at 2026-06-30) is ~33% of TTM revenue, so growth CONSUMES cash. Five-year reconciliation of NI+D&A+SBC vs OCF (FY2021-25) shows ~34c of every incremental revenue dollar absorbed; FY2025 alone was ~23c. wc_capture is -28% of the YoY revenue change in base and bear; -26% in bull to credit the FMI/Onsite inventory-management efficiency management describes.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial') with the adaptations file applied for the cyclical/lease/working-capital rules. First valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 = FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue +13.6%, operating margin 20.7%). Net cash and share count are from the Q2 2026 10-Q (2026-06-30), the latest filing. EBITDA margin driver is EBITDA/revenue with SBC inside EBITDA (FY2025 22.4% = operating income 20.2% + D&A 2.2%); SBC is then deducted separately at 0.10% of revenue. Horizon 10 years because revenue growth is still decelerating from 13% toward terminal through year 10 even though margins are flat by year 3. The terminal cap of 20x is non-binding in base (Gordon at 9%/3% = 17.2x) and is the house 'mature compounder' ceiling; the bear cap is 15x for a cyclical in a lower-growth world. Headline finding: at ~42x trailing earnings and ~55x owner FCF the price implies a forward IRR near 6%, well below the 9% WACC; see required_return_table.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: equity_5yr_cagr (7.61%), which ties to revenue 5yr 7.75% and split-adjusted EPS 5yr 7.90%; used as the ceiling the base path decelerates from (base 10-year average ~6.3%).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: 3-year equity CAGR (7.6%) is 38% above 3-year revenue CAGR (5.5%): FY2023-24 were a US industrial soft patch (revenue +5.2%, +2.7%) while retained earnings compounded; the 5-year figures are aligned within 0.3pp. Not a structural divergence.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped, see inputs). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.05pp because SBC is 0.1% of revenue: SBC is not eating cash-flow growth here. The 5-year FCF CAGR (2.35%) is depressed by the FY2020 base: $933.7M FCF on $859M net income was a COVID working-capital release (inventory drawdown) that then reversed in FY2021-22 (FCF $613M/$767M). Measured FY2019->FY2025 the owner-FCF CAGR is 9.7%. EPS CAGRs use net income / post-split share count because the CSV EPS column mixes pre- and post-split bases (FY2024 shows 2.01 on the pre-split basis; the 2:1 split was May 2024).

base.growth_note: FY2026: H1 +13.6%, Q2 daily sales +14.7% with ~290bps from pricing; H2 comps are tougher (Q3/Q4-25 grew 11-12%) so ~+12% H2 gives ~+13% for the year. Then decelerating from the 8% ten-year revenue CAGR to 3.5% as the current heavy-manufacturing/non-residential upcycle normalises and tariff-driven pricing fades.
base.ebitda_margin_note: FY2025 22.4% (operating margin 20.2% + D&A 2.2%); H1-2026 operating margin 20.7%, Q2 21.0%. Operating margin has sat between 20.0% and 20.8% every year FY2018-25: gross margin erodes ~75bps/yr from large-account mix and tariffs, SG&A leverage offsets it. Base holds that equilibrium with a 20bps lift for FY2026 evidence, to a 23.0% EBITDA / ~20.5% operating margin plateau.
base.capex_note: FY2026 guided $310-330M (~3.4% of ~$9.3B); FY2019-25 range 2.3-4.6%, median 3.0%. Capex above D&A (hub upgrades, trucking fleet, FMI devices) drifts D&A up from 2.2% to 2.5%.
base.cash_tax_note: FY2025 cash taxes paid $398.8M on pretax income $1,655M = 24.1%; provision 24.0%; FY2026 guidance ~24.6% ongoing. No NOLs, credits or valuation-allowance noise to ramp.

scenario_narratives.base: The current industrial upcycle (heavy manufacturing +18%, non-residential construction +17% in Q2 2026) carries FY2026 to ~+13%, then growth decelerates through the 8% ten-year average to 3.5% by year 10 as tariff-driven pricing (~290bps of Q2 growth) fades and FMI/Onsite signings settle at the 27-29k MEU run-rate. Gross margin keeps eroding ~75bps/yr from the deliberate national-account mix shift and higher-tariff inventory, and SG&A leverage keeps absorbing it, so the operating margin stays on its FY2018-25 plateau (~20.5%; 23% EBITDA). Working capital consumes ~28c of each incremental revenue dollar, capex runs at the guided ~3.4% then normalises to 3.0%. The new CEO (Watts, July 2026) executes the same three-pillar strategy. Owner FCF margin matures around 14% of revenue.
scenario_narratives.bull: Embedded Onsite/FMI infrastructure and the digital footprint (63-64% of sales) compound share gains against local distributors and Amazon Business: revenue grows 14% in FY2026 and holds 8-10% for four more years, helped by acquisitions that compress the international buildout to 2-3 years. Price/cost turns net positive as higher-tariff inventory is fully passed through, and national-account scale leverage lifts the EBITDA margin from 23.0% to 24.5% (operating margin ~22%). FMI data lets inventory turns improve, so growth consumes 26c rather than 28c per dollar. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects continued structural share gain in a fragmented MRO market.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 finishes at +11% as H2 daily sales slow, then the manufacturing PMI rolls over: revenue +1% in FY2027 and -4% in FY2028 (a moderate industrial recession, not 2009's -17%). The remaining ~40bps price-cost tariff headwind flows through on shrinking volume with 3-4x incremental margin impact, and the large-account mix continues to dilute gross margin without offsetting leverage, so the EBITDA margin falls from 22.4% to 20.5% at the trough and recovers only to 21% (operating margin ~18.5%, its worst since 2009). Amazon Business pressure on commoditised lines plus a CEO-transition wobble hold the recovery to 3-4%. Working capital releases cash in the down year (the model's negative capture on negative growth) which cushions but does not offset. Terminal growth 2%, cap 15x for a cyclical that has lost its margin premium.
scenario_narratives.shared: WACC 9.0% in every scenario: the difference between scenarios is in the flows, not the discount rate (risk charged once).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20% because Fastenal's daily sales track US manufacturing PMI, the stock has not yet seen a downcycle since the tariff regime began, and a CEO transition is two months old. Bull cut from 35% to 30% because it needs three independent things at once (the upcycle persisting, price-cost turning positive, and an M&A-accelerated international buildout that is so far only signalled). Base 50%: the FY2018-25 margin plateau is the best-evidenced feature of the company.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Fastenal is a genuinely high-quality compounder: no leverage, 30%+ ROIC, a physically embedded (Onsite/vending) moat, and an operating margin that has held 20-21% through every year since 2018. The DCF values that quality on its own cash flows: owner FCF is ~12.7% of revenue today and matures around 14%, discounted at 9%, with an unbinding 20x terminal cap. On those terms the weighted intrinsic value sits far below the market price. The gap is not a modelling artefact but the market's choice to capitalise ~55x owner FCF; the required_return_table shows what forward return the current price implies. The entry price at a 15% hurdle is well under half of intrinsic value, as the method warns for a slow-growing business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cyclical end markets: revenue tracks US manufacturing PMI and non-residential construction; the bear path assumes a moderate FY2027-28 recession, a 2009-style -17% would take the bear IV materially lower.
Gross margin erosion from national-account mix and tariffs outrunning SG&A leverage; each 1pp of sustained EBITDA margin is roughly $1.4/share of base value.
Working-capital intensity (~33% of revenue) means faster growth consumes more cash; the bull case is not linear in growth because of it.
Multiple compression: the price sits at ~42x trailing earnings; even the bull DCF does not reach it, so the equity's forward return depends on the multiple holding rather than on the cash flows.

Upside risk to the model: if the FMI/Onsite moat allows a structural EBITDA margin above 25% or growth above 8% for a decade, the base case is too conservative; the sensitivity grid and required-return table are the places to test that.
CEO transition (Jeff Watts from July 2026) and the pivot toward acquisitions for international expansion introduce capital-allocation risk a 60-year organic-growth record does not cover.
